newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots mixed.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots mixed.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed up across the board in very active trading mainly due to three new issues on the Shanghai and Shenzhen domestic A share markets, traders said.
The annual rate for the most active seven-day contract rose to 16.0 percent from 13.6 percent last Friday.
Total turnover on the six-contract market soared to 14.2 million lots from 4.86 million lots last Friday.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
Traders said the new issues pushed fund demand on the repo market up sharply.
"The new issues fanned fund demand, making many institutions borrow heavily on the repurchase market," said one trader.
The continued bull run on the A share markets was another positive factor pushing repo rates up today, traders said.
"The rates need a correction in the short term as they have become very high," said a second trader.
Contracts on Shanghai's T-bill spot market ended mixed on Monday with new A share issues and the bullish A share markets sucking more money out of the spot market, traders said.
The most actively traded 10-year bond that matures in June 2006, a market barometer, fell to 119.66 yuan from 120.05 yuan.
Combined volume of the seven-contract market rose slightly to 647,041 lots from 597,016 lots.
Traders said the spot market was unlikely to see any change in the short term with no sign of the A share markets ending their bull run in the short-term.
